assets.content:
Subject: Turn one IT procedure into a guide
Preview text: Try browser-based guide generation on Scribe’s free Basic plan.

Turn one browser procedure into a guide

Hi there,

If a browser-based IT procedure currently lives in one person’s head, perform it once and turn it into a how-to guide.

Scribe is documentation and workflow-capture software that turns actions taken in applications into step-by-step how-to guides your IT team can follow.

With Autocapture, Scribe turns work you have already performed into Scribes automatically. The procedure becomes a practical guide instead of a separate writing project.

The free Basic plan lets you generate how-to guides in the browser, so you can test one real procedure at no cost. Desktop application capture requires Pro or Enterprise.

Sign up and create a guide → https://scribehow.com/signup?plan=free

- Scribe

asset_metadata.single_idea: Take one browser-based IT procedure your team may currently carry in memory and turn it into a how-to guide with Scribe; the Basic plan lets you try browser guide generation for free.

selected_brief.selection_reason: This is the strongest supported first-use proposition for an IT buyer: it applies Scribe's documented capture mechanism to one concrete documentation task and gives the reader a free, browser-based way to judge the output without requiring procurement.

value_case.reader_benefit: If an IT procedure is currently carried in one person's head, the team can turn that performed work into a step-by-step guide instead of leaving the procedure undocumented.
value_case.mechanism: Scribe's Autocapture turns work already performed into Scribes automatically, while the free Basic plan supports generating how-to guides in the browser.
decision_conditions: The free Basic use described here is browser-based.
Capturing processes in desktop applications requires Pro or Enterprise.

claim_conditions: Frame tribal knowledge as a conditional situation; P1 is based on a single historical source and does not establish that every recipient has this problem.
Do not imply that desktop capture is included in Basic.
Do not state that Autocapture itself is a Basic-plan entitlement; the evidence establishes the capability and separately establishes free browser-based guide generation.
Free Basic plan covers browser-based guide generation only (E1)
Capturing processes in desktop applications requires Pro or Enterprise (E5)
Team-level plan tiers apply if the buyer later adds teammates (E7, E6)
Do not promise: No claim that steps are captured as screenshots
Do not promise: No claim that guides stay current when systems change
Do not promise: No claim that output is usable as structured context for internal AI tools
Do not promise: No claim of zero disruption, headcount reduction, growth or replacement of an incumbent tool
Do not promise: No claim about time saved or mistakes avoided for this buyer
Not established: Step captures include screenshots of each step
Not established: Procedures are kept current when the underlying systems change
Not established: Captured procedures are reusable as structured context for internal AI tools
This is a documented-use draft, not proof of the broader audience hypothesis or recipient fit.

Problem P1 is an inferred audience hypothesis: Some staff at technology companies report that unwritten, undocumented knowledge ('tribal knowledge') held by individuals is common and seen as important, with documentation often not treated as a first-class deliverable. Use it only conditionally (if this is relevant to the reader), not as a known current pain, behavior or outcome of the recipient. Product fit does not establish current demand or a demonstrated customer outcome.
Historical sources (2019-07-31); present applicability is not corroborated.
Single-source problem; independent corroboration is not established.

The mechanism documents automatic conversion of completed work into guides, but the problem itself rests on a single 2019 forum thread about technology-company staff whose present applicability is uncorroborated, and no selected evidence shows documentation becoming a first-class deliverable.
selected_brief.job: Make a new IT buyer want to use Scribe for one real procedure and click to try browser-based guide generation for free.
selected_brief.single_idea: Take one browser-based IT procedure your team may currently carry in memory and turn it into a how-to guide with Scribe; the Basic plan lets you try browser guide generation for free.
selected_brief.felt_need: Some staff at technology companies report that unwritten, undocumented knowledge ('tribal knowledge') held by individuals is common and seen as important, with documentation often not treated as a first-class deliverable.
selected_brief.mechanism: Scribe's Autocapture turns work already performed into Scribes automatically. For the first test, Basic lets the reader generate a how-to guide in the browser at no cost; desktop application capture is reserved for Pro and Enterprise.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: This is a credible alternative when an IT buyer's first concern is exposing sensitive information during workflow capture: it leads with the documented redaction mechanism and sends the reader to public IT documentation before asking them to create an account.
